solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First stronghold to protect an indefinite number after retreat

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and guard it, so one piece wraps round the other
a retreat is a going backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a fort is a stronghold
'some' names an unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: A castle comes first, guarding a handful of troops after they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like an adjective opening the scene, but it is the definition; the indefinite number turns round before the stronghold closes over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foremost comes at the very front or ranks highest, which is what being first means.

clue.text: Confronts having to collect ash container — they may be very hot

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece takes the other inside

blocks.note: to face someone is to confront them
an urn holds a person's ashes

explanation.surface: Someone is made to go and fetch the urn of ashes after a cremation.
explanation.walkthrough: The container splits after its first letter to hold the vessel for ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Furnaces are enclosed chambers for heating metal or buildings, so they run at extremely high temperatures.

clue.text: Man perhaps writing half of the letters

indicators.note: taking half of a word means dropping the rest of it

blocks.note: writing is one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
the letters make up the alphabet, and its first half is kept

explanation.surface: Someone is writing out the first half of the alphabet, like a child at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' of basic schooling are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so any of them can give R. ALPHABET has eight letters; half is ALPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a common male first name, so it is one example of a man; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: A line became hard to sort out, as only fit for computer input?

indicators.note: sorting out a jumble means rearranging it into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A line of text grew so hard to decipher that only a computer could manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'A line became hard' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Data that is machine-readable is in a form a computer can process directly, often not easily read by people.

clue.text: Son — little couple’s beloved one

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
wee is Scottish for small
to couple is to tie together

explanation.surface: The son of a small pair is their darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a noun for two people, but it is the verb meaning to join, giving TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetie is an affectionate term of address for a loved person, a darling.

clue.text: Something surgeon provides for pain

blocks.note: first meaning: a loop of thread closing a wound
second meaning: a sharp pain in the side, as when running

explanation.surface: A surgeon hands out something to relieve pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests painkillers; instead the surgeon's item and the pain are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons close wounds with sutures, and a sudden cramp under the ribs during exercise has the same name.

clue.text: Mad golfer keen to wed — a temptation that should have been avoided?

definitions.text: a temptation that should have been avoided

indicators.note: madness scrambles things, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A golfer desperate to marry is chasing a temptation he should have steered clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'golfer keen to wed' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve were forbidden to eat from this tree in Eden, and yielding to it caused the Fall.

clue.text: Parent upset over boy getting cut in the head

indicators.note: something upset is knocked into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An upset parent watches over a boy who has cut his head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second. Ned is a stock crossword boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan is to bore a hole in the skull surgically, so a trepanned patient has been cut in the head.

clue.text: Instruction to give girl corporal punishment here?

blocks.note: hitting someone is physical punishment, here given as an order
a girl is referred to as her

explanation.surface: A grim order to beat a girl on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a command, HIT HER, and the question mark flags that the result also means 'here'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hither is an old-fashioned adverb meaning to this place, as in 'come hither'.

clue.text: Great big bully pursuing maiden in the capital

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so this part is placed later in the answer

blocks.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
OS stands for outsize, very large
to cow is to bully into submission

explanation.surface: A huge thug is chasing a young woman through the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M; OS is the clothing-size label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia, so it is one example of a capital.

clue.text: Artefact of Catholic priest being held?

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: An object belonging to a Catholic priest who has been taken captive.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel, is the setters' favourite priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, an artefact of historical or religious interest.

clue.text: Bound to take chaps into extraterrestrial sort of escape

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: to lope is to move with long bounding strides
chaps are men
ET is the extraterrestrial from the film

explanation.surface: An alien spacecraft is sure to abduct some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', but it is the verb for leaping; the leap and the chaps join up before going inside the alien.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is running away secretly to marry, one particular kind of getaway.

clue.text: The fellow is entertained by Greek following rationalist philosophy?

indicators.note: a guest who is entertained is taken in by the host, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a fellow is he
taken as written
Attic is the Greek of ancient Athens

explanation.surface: A man is hosted by a Greek who follows a school of reasoned philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic is the dialect of classical Athens, so it serves for 'Greek'. The question mark admits that rationalism need not mean godlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism rejects belief in gods on grounds of reason and evidence, a stance often tied to rationalist thought.

clue.text: Language of love used by wise man

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A sage speaks the language of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis scoring, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Osage is the Siouan tongue of the Osage Nation, a Native American people of Oklahoma.

clue.text: Stand where gateman has returned

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the letters lie held within the words
something returned goes back the way it came, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the man at the gate stands now he is back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'whERE GATEman' to find the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a piece of furniture with open shelves for displaying ornaments, a kind of display stand.

clue.text: Cigars given out with ale and port

indicators.note: things given out are distributed and scattered, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: After dinner the host hands round cigars, ale and a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' at the end looks like the fortified wine, going with the cigars and ale; it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeciras is a Spanish harbour city on the bay facing Gibraltar, a major seaport.

clue.text: A top man, weak initially, is getting aroused

indicators.note: initially points to what comes at the very start, so only an opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A feeble leader is finally being stirred into action.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks run in answer order: the initial letter first, then A KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Waking is coming out of sleep, and to arouse someone in the old sense is to wake them.

clue.text: Dry area sinking into sea somewhere across the Channel

indicators.note: sinking into something means going down inside it

blocks.note: the briny is a name for the sea
TT means teetotal, off alcohol
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A patch of dry land slips beneath the waves somewhere off the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means not drinking, not arid: TT stands for teetotal. 'The briny' is an old jocular name for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittany is the region of north-west France facing England over the English Channel.

clue.text: Old soldiers being gathered came to the same conclusion

indicators.note: being gathered means drawn in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: aged means old
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Veterans assembled at a reunion all reached the same verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers' reads as veterans, but the two words work separately, the first wrapping round the second. The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: People who agreed reached a shared view, each arriving at the same judgement.

clue.text: Minimal length after incompetent person cut cloth

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so a final letter is lopped off
coming after means being placed later, so this piece goes at the end

blocks.note: a duffer is a bungler
L is the shortest form of length, a single letter

explanation.surface: A bungler has cut the cloth far too short.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFFER loses its last letter, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Duffel is a coarse heavy woollen fabric with a thick nap, used for coats and bags.

clue.text: Food Rosy brought around as a possible first course?

indicators.note: bringing something around turns it to face the other way

blocks.note: chow is slang for food
rosy means red

explanation.surface: A girl named Rosy carries round the dishes at the start of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosy' looks like a name, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, often of clams or fish, and soup is often served as a starter.

clue.text: Investigator given a ring in awkward situation

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: being in a corner is being in a tight spot
a ring is shaped like O

explanation.surface: A detective gets a phone call while in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a ring' sounds like a phone call; it is the letter O going inside CORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is an official who holds inquests into violent, sudden or unexplained deaths.

clue.text: Not half thin, like many a birthday cake cut up

indicators.note: without half of it, only part of the word survives

blocks.note: slim means thin
birthday cakes are usually iced

explanation.surface: A birthday cake gets cut up into thin portions, not halves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it literally removes half of the word for thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sliced has been cut into pieces, divided with a knife.

clue.text: Oxford will always be beaten

definitions.note: a verbal phrase ending in a past participle, with the answer completing it

blocks.note: first meaning: an Oxford is a shoe fastened with strings
second meaning: thrashed, as in given a lacing

explanation.surface: Oxford is doomed to lose, presumably in the Boat Race against Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about the university; the first meaning is the Oxford shoe, a style that always ties up.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford shoe is always fastened with strings, and to lace someone is dated slang for giving them a beating.

clue.text: Glow of one about to engage in 11?

indicators.note: to engage in something is to enter into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
re means about, concerning
the answer at 11 across is a running away, a flight

explanation.surface: The glow on someone about to run off with their lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to ELOPEMENT, an escape, so the cross-reference stands for a synonym of that answer rather than the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Firelight is the light cast by a fire, the warm glow of flames in a hearth.

clue.text: Delighted to take in Jehan’s last for organ

indicators.note: last points to the end, so only a final letter is kept
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: glad means delighted
the closing letter of the name

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to hear the end of Jehan's organ recital.
explanation.walkthrough: Jehan Alain was a French organist-composer, which is why the name suits the surface; only its final letter goes inside GLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland is a bodily organ that secretes substances such as hormones.

clue.text: Conservative head receiving a guy who lives on an island?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a person, the answer used as a noun

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
bean is slang for the head
to guy is to tease, and to rib means the same

explanation.surface: A Tory leader welcomes a man who lives on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative head' looks like a party leader, but it splits into C and BEAN, with A RIB between. 'Guy' is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean is a person from the West Indian islands, which is why the question mark hedges.

clue.text: Part of America with no room for trendy goddess

indicators.note: having no room for something means leaving it out

blocks.note: Indiana is a US state
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Somewhere in America has no room for a fashionable goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: INDIANA drops its opening IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman deity of hunting and the moon, counterpart of the Greek Artemis.

clue.text: One going quickly turning miserable, star losing love

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the opposite way
to lose something is to be left without it

blocks.note: sad means miserable
the star of a story is its hero
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A celebrity whose romance has ended is quickly becoming unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD turns to DAS; HERO without O is HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dasher is someone who dashes, rushing along at speed; it is also one of Santa's reindeer.

clue.text: Diner travelling in carriage prepared to talk to fellow passengers?

definitions.text: prepared to talk to fellow passengers

indicators.note: travelling means on the move, so the letters shift into a new order
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a fly is a light one-horse carriage

explanation.surface: A diner riding in a railway carriage is open to chatting with others on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a train, but it is FLY, an old horse-drawn cab hired by the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly person is sociable and happy to chat, as a talkative traveller would be.
